title: Fireside ops retrospective + bottleneck mapping — Nov 3, 2026
content:
Purpose: synthesize topics from the engineering all-hands (Nov 3), capture cross-team bottlenecks, and produce a short prioritized action list. This was an intentionally conversational, "fireside" format: fewer slides, more candid status checks. Notes below are a mix of speaker highlights, attendee questions, and quick follow-ups (things to act on in the next 2 sprints).

Attendees: eng-serving-runtime + reprs from infra, SRE, platform-eng, product-hosted-api, observability. ~45 people total.

Top-line summary:
- Overall health: Stable but capacity-constrained on several Dedicated GPU pools. Latency SLOs met for 95th across most models, but 99th tail stretches during evening peak in eu-west-1.
- Primary recurring theme: cascade from model-variant sprawl -> routing policy complexity -> cache miss amplification -> GPU saturation.
- Tone: collaborative; strong requests for tooling to map dependent flows (which routes touch which model variants).

Key updates (by area):
1) Serving runtime (Miguel)
- Rollout of KV prefix cache sharding experiment (canary on dedicated-1) reduced per-token compute by ~6% on average for matched workloads. Initial telemetry looks promising, but we saw one regression: a cache eviction thrash when traffic pattern changed unexpectedly on Oct 27. Root cause: eviction window tuned for uniform keys; not for bursty prefix patterns.
- Action: adjust eviction thresholds and add adaptive sampling (owner: Miguel; target: 2026-11-10).

2) Routing & model catalog (Asha)
- Catalog cleanup: removed 12 legacy variants not used in last 90 days. But some internal teams still reference them in config — leading to silent fallbacks.
- Plan: implement a warning system during config deploys and a stale-variant telemetry dashboard. (owner: Asha; draft design by Nov 12).

3) Dedicated capacity & infra (Jordan)
- Capacity: two Dedicated pools are at 92–96% sustained utilization; eviction/fallbacks increased 2x during last spike. Forecast: Q4 holiday traffic could push eu-west-1 past 100% in certain windows.
- Short-term mitigation: enable controlled burst cushions and prioritize critical customer routes. (owner: Jordan; implement by Nov 8)
- Mid-term: procure extra reserved capacity for eu-west-1 or enable cross-region spillover for low-latency non-critical jobs. (owner: infra; plan by Nov 24).

4) Observability & console (Priya)
- New per-request KV hitrate breakdown landed in staging. Early feedback: helpful but noisy; need aggregation by Route+Model+Session.
- Quick ask: add toggle to show recent TTL/eviction history for a given key prefix. (owner: Priya; POC by Nov 15).

Discussion highlights / Q&A:
- Q: Why do some routes suddenly map to very large sequence lengths? A: Some clients started sending dense context (full chat history) instead of a delta. Product to publish guidance on client-side trimming. (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Q: Can we auto-fallback to a quantized variant when GPU saturation detected? A: Yes — routing policy supports compatible variants; need guardrails for quality. Proposed: automatic fallback with a quality monitor and immediate rollback if eval signal drops >5% on a prompt set. (owner: model-onboarding + runtime; experiment Nov 15).

Bottleneck map (prioritized):
1) Cache eviction thrash on bursty prefixes -> causes extra compute and higher latency spikes. (severity: high)
2) Catalog drift (stale model variants referenced by configs) -> causes silent fallbacks and confusing metrics. (severity: high)
3) Dedicated pool saturation in eu-west-1 at evening peak -> customer risk. (severity: high)
4) Telemetry cardinality noise -> hard to quickly diagnose per-route problems (severity: medium)
5) Client-side context bloat -> increases sequence lengths and cost (severity: medium)

Decisions made during meeting:
- Short-term: Enable conservative cross-region spillover for non-SLA-critical requests by Nov 8 (Jordan).
- Telemetry: roll forward per-request KV hitrate but add 1-hour aggregations and a UI filter to reduce noise (Priya).
- Model variant deprecation policy: enforce a 2-stage warning (config-deploy warning + automated email to owners) before hard deletion. (Asha).

Action items (owner — due):
- Miguel: implement adaptive eviction thresholds + chaos test for bursty prefixes — due 2026-11-10.
- Jordan: enable controlled burst cushions + emergency spillover route — due 2026-11-08.
- Asha: prototype stale-variant deploy warning & dashboard wireframe — due 2026-11-12.
- Priya: POC for TTL/eviction history toggle in console + aggregate views — due 2026-11-15.
- Product-hosted-api: publish best-practices doc for client-side context trimming + 2 sample SDK helpers — due 2026-11-17.
- Model-onboarding: design automatic fallback + quality monitor experiment (A/B) — experiment ready 2026-11-15.

Risks & mitigation notes:
- If capacity forecast underestimates traffic, customers on Dedicated may see degraded throughput; mitigation: communicate potential limited maintenance window and offer temporary routing to nearby region. (SRE playbook update: Jordan + SRE; due 2026-11-06).
- Automatic fallback to quantized variants could cause subtle quality regressions for long-tail prompts; we will gate by a small eval suite and incremental rollout.

Parking lot (items pushed for later):
- Deep investigation of 99.99th tail: requires full tracing + kernel level telemetry (research spike Q1 2027).
- Long-term: smarter shard placement for KV caches tied to client geography (proposal by platform-eng in Dec).

Notes to self / informal bits captured during discussion:
- Several folks mentioned confusion over model names in the catalog UI (short names vs. model hashes). Small UX win: show both and a tooltip with model lineage. (low effort).
- Wanted: a simple "simulate traffic" UI where product/solutions can check how changes to routing or variants would affect a sample customer. Could be a follow-up hackathon project.

Next check-in: quick status sync in the serving-runtime weekly standup on 2026-11-09. Full retrospective follow-up with artifacts on Confluence and a short executive summary by 2026-11-18.

If you see anything missing or incorrect, add a comment below or ping me in Slack (linnea.c).
